title: The rundown
note: What's going on right now, in one place. The ↗ links out to the original source; the item's own text turns into a link only once it becomes a full entry here.

items.text: President Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire," but Ukraine's Zelensky said Russia had already violated it with a strike on a Kharkiv power plant, calling the announcement "news to me."

A year after the Gaza ceasefire took effect, Al Jazeera reports Israeli forces have kept moving the buffer "Yellow Line" farther west, leaving nearly two-thirds of Gaza under Israeli military control or access restrictions.

Wall Street closed last week at record highs — the Dow at 51,654.95, the S&P 500 at 7,811.54 and the Nasdaq at 27,366.17 on Friday — with Monday's futures flat ahead of bank earnings season and lingering worries about an AI bubble and elevated Treasury yields.
Bitcoin traded around $83,000 to $84,000 Monday, still well below the $126,210.50 all-time high it hit on October 6, 2025, with traders watching Wednesday's September inflation data.

Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, cutting short-prompt pricing to $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens from Haiku 4.5's $1/$5 while reporting a jump to 72.4% on the OSWorld 2.1 computer-use benchmark, up from 15.7%.

Google announced its Gemini 4 Argon flagship model on September 30, giving cybersecurity partners first access at introductory API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with no public release date set yet.

Underwater archaeologists recovered a bronze signet ring engraved with the Lighthouse of Alexandria from the sunken island of Antirhodos in Alexandria's Eastern Harbour — the first known seal ring depicting the lost wonder, Egypt's Supreme Council of Antiquities said.

The FDA approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq) plus chemotherapy on October 8 for stage III colon cancer with deficient DNA mismatch repair, based on the ATOMIC trial's finding of a 50% reduction in recurrence or death risk among 711 adult patients.

A Vanderbilt-led study published October 8 in JAMA Otolaryngology found that genetic risk scores built from detailed hearing-test data on 16,000 BioVU biobank participants predicted hearing loss better than scores built from diagnostic billing codes alone.

Universal's horror release "Other Mommy" won the weekend box office with an estimated $27.5 million from 3,365 theaters, while Amazon MGM's "Verity" fell 64.5% in its second weekend to about $11.5 million for second place.
Sony's "The Social Reckoning" bombed in its opening weekend, debuting in fifth place with just $5.5 million.
